name: The Queue at the Shelter
story: A queue stands where the roof used to be, and it has not moved since morning.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The queue starts at a cracked post and ends at a door with no roof above it. Nobody has moved since morning.

beforeStory.speaker: Waiting Traveller
beforeStory.text: I am first. I have been first since the second day, and I am not moving for anyone.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith sets his pack down behind the last porter and stands in line. The porters lift their loads and set them down again.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The line closes where Arith stood. The traveller at the front looks back once, then faces the door again.

afterStory.speaker: Waiting Traveller
afterStory.text: If it opens, call my name first. I have been here long enough.

name: One More Turn
story: The queue offers Arith one more turn at the front, if he comes to it with nobody and nothing.

beforeStory.speaker: Waiting Traveller
beforeStory.text: One more turn. You go up alone, and you carry nothing in your hands.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith sets his pack against the post and steps away from the others. His hands stay open at his sides.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The porters step back to let him through. The door is closer than it was, and still shut.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The turn ends at the door. Arith puts his palm flat on the wood and leans until his arm shakes.

afterStory.speaker: Waiting Traveller
afterStory.text: Come back at first light. I will keep the next turn for you.

name: The Weight
story: The ferry master weighs every traveller, and offers to carry what is too heavy.

beforeStory.speaker: Ferry Master
beforeStory.text: Put it all on the scale. Everything you mean to carry across goes on the scale first.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith steps onto the plate. The needle swings past the mark and stays there.

beforeStory.speaker: Ferry Master
beforeStory.text: I can take the weight. It goes into the boat, not into you.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The ferry master writes the number in a small book and closes it. Arith lifts his own weight again and carries it down to the water.

afterStory.speaker: Ferry Master
afterStory.text: You will feel it at the far bank. Come back if you want it carried the rest of the way.

name: The Bench Repaired
story: Someone is mending one end of the white bench, and the shelter will not let the work finish.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: A carpenter kneels at the end of the white bench with a new plank across his knees. Three helpers hold the old boards down.

beforeStory.speaker: Carpenter
beforeStory.text: Every time I set the last nail, someone sits on it. Hold them back a moment longer.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith stands at the end of the bench with his back to the queue. The queue comes anyway.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The nail goes in. The bench sits level, and the queue takes the repaired end as if it had always been there.

afterStory.speaker: Carpenter
afterStory.text: Do not let them move it. Not until the joint sets.

name: Two Coats
story: Two coats lie on the repaired bench, and the rain has not touched either of them.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Two coats on the bench. One is folded small, the way a coat is folded when its owner means to come back for it.

beforeStory.speaker: Helper
beforeStory.text: Do not touch the folded one. He will want it dry.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith sits at the open end of the bench. He keeps his hands off the folded coat.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: Arith folds the open coat and lays it beside the other. The two are the same size.

afterStory.speaker: Helper
afterStory.text: Leave them both. He will come back for his, and then I will know which one is mine.

name: Fare for One
story: The ferry takes one passenger, and the ferryman has not reached the far bank in years.

beforeStory.speaker: Ferryman
beforeStory.text: Fare for one. There is room for one in the boat, and the water does not ask who.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith steps down into the boat. The ferryman pushes off without looking at the shore.

beforeStory.speaker: Ferryman
beforeStory.text: Sit in the middle and do not trail your hand in the water. We are close now.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The current turns the boat and sets it back against the same post. The ferryman ships the oars.

afterStory.speaker: Ferryman
afterStory.text: Same time tomorrow. If you find the far bank before I do, wait for me there.
